_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The sower went out to scatter the seed.
Some on the path, some on the rock, some in good soil.
Your word is a lamp to our feet.
A light to the road we walk.
Let the one with ears to hear, listen.
Open us, and let the seed take root.
Come, let us worship the God who plants.
We come; sow your word in us. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture the field at dawn, the sower's arm swinging wide, seed flying onto path and rock and rich dark ground.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow.
Some of us came hard-packed as a footpath, some shallow over stone, some choked by the week's thorns.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow.
But the sower is not stingy — he flings the seed everywhere, on every kind of ground, hoping.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow.
Your word is a lamp to our feet; let it fall on good soil today and bear thirty, sixty, a hundredfold.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow. Amen and amen!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The sower scatters seed on every kind of ground.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow.
Some of us are footpath, some stone, some thorns.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow.
Your word is a lamp to our feet on the road.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow.
Come, let us worship the God who plants in us.
Sow your word in us, and let it grow. Amen.
